svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: a framework update keeps lychee reading its settings, and the project's own addresses stay in a file of their own
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: a framework update keeps lychee reading its settings, and the project's own addresses stay in a file

g.text: Given the developer kept their own accepted status codes in the
toolbox's lychee settings, and their own address in .lycheeignore
Off camera, the project was generated from release 23.0.43 of a test toolbox, whose lychee
settings, .config/lychee/config.toml, end on the exclude_path list. Its MegaLinter settings
run lychee alone, on docs/services.md, so the run stays short.
On screen, the developer's commit, "docs: link our local services". At the top of the
toolbox's lychee settings, an accept list names the status codes lychee must count as a
working link: 200 (OK), 206, 403 (forbidden) and 429 (too many requests). The storage console
address goes in .lycheeignore, a file of the project's own. docs/services.md links to that
console and to http://127.0.0.2:9/status, where nothing answers.
When the developer updates the project to the release that adds the toolbox's own accept
list
Release 24.4.10 of the test toolbox adds its own accept list at the end of the same file. Copier says "Updating to
template version 24.4.10" and merges it without a conflict, so the file now sets accept twice, which TOML refuses.
Copier then runs the release's migration, merge-lychee-keys.py, which prints "[lychee migration] accept was set twice in
.config/lychee/config.toml: merged into one list".
Then the lychee settings keep one accept list, with the developer's
codes and the toolbox's
What the update changed in the lychee settings. The developer's list leaves the top of the
file. At the end, under the toolbox's explanation, one list holds the developer's 200, 206,
403 and 429 and the toolbox's '200..=299'.
Just above, the release says where a project's own addresses go from now on: .lycheeignore, a
file no update touches.
And lychee reads its settings, skips the address in .lycheeignore and reports the dead link
The developer runs MegaLinter and, as it fails, reads lychee's own report. lychee read its settings and checked the two
links of docs/services.md: Excluded counts 1, the storage console that .lycheeignore lists, and Errors counts 1.
That error is the dead link, http://127.0.0.2:9/status, refused because nothing answers there. lychee checks links
again, and the project's own address stays out of the check.
